Create one character reference sheet from <Picture 1>.
Preserve the same character design and rendering style across all views.
White background. Each requested view appears once.
Preserve the character’s natural body surface, colors, markings and body structure from <Picture 1>. Keep the visible torso and lower body free of garments. Retain compatible accessories.
Use the same stance and limb arrangement as <Picture 1> across all three full-body views. Place the six portraits in the two columns on the left, the three full-body views in the middle, and the hand and foot close-ups in the column on the right. Within each column, read top to bottom:
Front portrait with the complete head and upper chest. / Profile portrait facing image-left, with the complete head and upper chest. / Three-quarter portrait facing image-left, with the complete head and upper chest.
Profile portrait facing image-right, with the complete head and upper chest. / Three-quarter portrait facing image-right, with the complete head and upper chest. / Portrait directly from behind, with the complete head and upper back.
One complete front view in the character’s natural stance, including the entire silhouette.
Full body in profile facing image-right. Turn the same figure in place, keeping the reference pose and the same weight-bearing limbs.
One complete view directly from behind in the character’s natural stance, including the entire silhouette.
One close-up of the character’s hands or forepaws as shown in the reference. Keep their shape and surface markings. Retain reference hand coverings when present. / One close-up of the character’s feet or hind paws as shown in the reference. Keep their shape and surface markings. Retain reference footwear when present.
